key_trends: Shift towards value-based pricing over hourly billing
Increased adoption of AI for document automation and research
Consolidation of boutique firms by private equity-backed platforms
Focus on ESG and sustainability advisory services
regulatory_factors: Potential changes to UK audit and corporate governance standards
GDPR and data privacy requirements for client data
observations: The UK professional services sector remains a global leader but faces domestic margin pressure due to wage inflation.
Business consulting is increasingly bifurcated between high-end strategy and commoditised implementation.

competitive_positioning.positioning_assessment: As a boutique advisory firm with no public revenue data, Cooper Gibson likely operates in the micro-to-small segment. These firms typically rely on high-touch partner relationships and niche expertise but face challenges in scalability and owner-dependency.

factors_affecting_multiple: Quality of recurring revenue vs one-off project fees
premium_factors: Niche expertise in high-barrier sectors (e.g., Life Sciences, Fintech)
discount_factors: High dependency on the founder for business development
Small headcount (<10) limiting capacity for growth

growth_opportunities.description: Converting bespoke advisory into scalable digital toolkits or subscription-based insights to reduce labour dependency.
Partnering with complementary firms (e.g., accounting or legal) to create a cross-referral ecosystem.

sector_risks.description: High competition for skilled consultants leading to wage inflation and margin erosion.
Discretionary consulting spend is often the first budget cut during corporate belt-tightening.

key_findings: The business likely falls into the 2.0x - 3.5x EBITDA range typical for UK SME professional services.
Valuation will be heavily sensitive to the 'stickiness' of the client base and the level of founder involvement.
M&A activity in this space is currently driven by larger firms seeking niche expertise or 'acqui-hires'.
narrative: Cooper Gibson operates in a mature and highly fragmented UK consulting market. Without specific financial data, the company is assessed as a boutique player. In the UK SME market, such firms are valued conservatively due to high 'key person' risk and the project-based nature of the work. To achieve a multiple at the higher end of the 2.0x-3.5x range, the buyer would need to see evidence of multi-year contracts and a management team capable of operating independently of the current owners.
